note: DRAFT positional playbook for professional/IT services agreements governed by Indian law. Covers payment terms, liability cap, IP ownership, termination, warranty, governing law, data protection, and SLA uptime. No in-house lawyer has approved these positions.
applies_to: Professional services, IT services, and consulting agreements for Indian companies
not_legal_advice: Every finding is a POTENTIAL_ISSUE against a company standard, not a statement of law.

rules.why: Payment terms. 30 days is standard for professional services; 45-60 for enterprise. Above 90 days is cash-flow hostile.
Liability cap as multiple of monthly fees. 12x (annual contract value) is standard. Below 1 month renders the contract commercially non-viable as a risk allocation mechanism.

starting.text: Client owns deliverables, vendor retains pre-existing IP

fallbacks.text: Joint ownership with unrestricted license to client

rules.why: IP ownership of deliverables. Client ownership with vendor retaining pre-existing IP/tools is standard. Vendor-owns-all is unusual for custom work.
Termination for convenience notice period. 30 days is standard. Longer periods protect the vendor's resource allocation.
Post-delivery warranty period for defect correction. 90 days is market standard for IT services. No warranty at all is a dealbreaker.
Services rendered in India should be governed by Indian law. Avoids jurisdictional complexity for dispute resolution.

starting.text: SPDI Rules compliance + data processing agreement

fallbacks.text: Reasonable security practices per IT Act s.43A

rules.why: Data protection obligations. SPDI Rules 2011 (under IT Act s.43A) are the current standard for handling sensitive personal data in India. When DPDP Act 2023 rules are notified, this will need updating.
SLA uptime commitment for hosted/SaaS services. 99.9% is industry standard (8.76 hrs downtime/year). Below 95% (18.25 days/year) is commercially unacceptable.
